findings.rootCause: LmdbSailStore.refreshFrontierStatisticsDelta mapped every typed delta failure except CONFIDENCE_TOO_WIDE to RETRY: the envelope failure 'Frontier signed-delta publication exceeds its persistent envelope' (MEMORY_PRESSURE from FrontierStatisticsDeltaBuilder.validateDiskBudget), the layer-limit throw, the dimension-overflow throw and the plain IOException FrontierOmniDeltaBuilder raised on an Omni dimension mismatch. runScheduledFrontierRebuild returned on RETRY before the base-rebuild branch and its finally block rescheduled every estimatorPersistDelayMillis (1 s), so a deterministic failure repeated forever. Nothing triggered a base rebuild before the delta tier hit its structural ceiling (disk/16: 1 MiB at 16 MiB, 32 MiB at the 512 MiB default; the compactor retains every mutation, ~300 B each, so the tier grows monotonically since the last base). -Xmx drift changes FrontierStatisticsBuildConfig.cellCount, so after a restart every delta failed with the dimension mismatch. Reproduced with real LmdbStores: permanent stall after 32k inserts at 16 MiB and after 112,000 inserts at the default budget; restart with a different budget never recovered.
findings.change: (1) Typed permanence: FrontierStatisticsException gained a `permanent` flag with requiresBaseRebuild(), two new ctors (existing ctors keep transient semantics) and permanent()/transientFailure() factories. FrontierStatisticsDeltaBuilder marks the envelope, layer-limit and dimension-overflow throws permanent; FrontierOmniDeltaBuilder throws a permanent FrontierStatisticsException(MEMORY_PRESSURE) instead of a plain IOException on dimension mismatch (critique issue[9]: MEMORY_PRESSURE, not SHARD_CORRUPT, so recovery diagnostics are not conflated). (2) LmdbSailStore.classifyDeltaFailure + FrontierRebuildSchedulePolicy.deltaFailureRequiresBaseRebuild (pure, unit-tested): permanent or CONFIDENCE_TOO_WIDE -> BASE_REBUILD_REQUIRED at once; transient failures RETRY up to FRONTIER_MAX_TRANSIENT_DELTA_FAILURES=8 for the same covered sequence, then escalate with one WARN; the counter resets on a successful publish. (3) Insertion-debt trigger frontierBaseRefreshOverdue(status), evaluated only AFTER a successful delta publish (critique issue[5], major: never before building, so deltas keep flowing while the rebuild is pending): delta tier >= FRONTIER_DELTA_TIER_REBUILD_FRACTION (0.75) * deltaAndManifestBudgetBytes, or deleteDebt >= 0.10 (existing), or the dimension-mismatch flag. The same predicate keeps the equivalent-generation abort shortcut in rebuildFrontierStatisticsV2 from skipping an overdue base. (4) Dimension check at open: frontierOmniDimensionsDiffer(service, buildConfig) compares the current manifest's width/depth/design/audit lanes (via the new LmdbStatisticsService.currentManifest()) with the configured budgets; a mismatch sets frontierDimensionRebuildRequired, which is treated like service.rebuildRequired() in init and in runScheduledFrontierRebuild and is cleared by clearFrontierBaseRebuildPending() after a successful base publish. Sound because base rebuilds fold all deltas into a fresh base, so the envelope failure becomes exceptional rather than the steady state; the 0.75 fraction does not fire for a single small delta (guarded by LmdbFrontierStoreLifecycleTest#committedMutationPublishesSignedDeltaWithoutRebuildingBase in the module suite). Design deviation stated: the debt trigger runs after publish instead of 'before building and after publish', per the critique's coupling argument; the mismatch reason is MEMORY_PRESSURE instead of the design's SHARD_CORRUPT. Critique issue[5] (major: debt trigger must run only after a successful publish) and issue[9] (minor: MEMORY_PRESSURE, not SHARD_CORRUPT) are both implemented and covered by deltaTierDebtRebuildsBaseWhileSmallCommitsContinue / FrontierDeltaPermanentFailureTest#omniDimensionMismatchIsATypedPermanentFailure. Test-only change this session (module-suite triage): deltaTierDebtRebuildsBaseWhileSmallCommitsContinue's 'uncovered window < 10 s' guard fired at 15.5 s in the suite run under load 35 while its fix assertions (base rebuilt, caught up, lastFailure empty) passed; the window was the base rebuild's own execution on the single-threaded estimatorPersistExec, during which no delta can publish by design. The guard now measures only uncovered windows in which no base-build phase (PASS_ONE/PASS_TWO/COMPACTING/PUBLISHING) was observed, i.e. exactly the critique's concern that deltas keep flowing while the rebuild is PENDING; a status timeline is appended to every failure message and the outer loop bound is 40 s. Under the design's 'before building' variant this guard still fails (deltas stop while pending). findings.rootCause: Every commit called LmdbSailStore.requestFrontierRebuild(), resetting frontierRebuildRequestedNanos; runScheduledFrontierRebuild started a base rebuild only when frontierRebuildQuietPeriodElapsed() (>= estimatorPersistDelayMillis = 1 s since the LAST request) with no upper bound, and its finally block forced RETRY whenever the request stamp moved. Under >= 1 commit/s a required base rebuild was deferred indefinitely. Because a 20,000-row transaction exceeded MAXIMUM_IN_MEMORY_MUTATIONS (16,384) the tail was cleared and completeTransactionPrefix returned empty (BASE_REBUILD_REQUIRED), so the starved base rebuild was the only path to coverage: covered sequence stayed 0 for 12 s at 4 commits/s and the 20k-row predicate stayed FrontierLeafEstimate[pointRows=1.0, fallbackReason=CONFIDENCE_TOO_WIDE]. The old code also returned on a delta RETRY before reaching the base-rebuild branch, so a pending base rebuild and delta publication blocked each other.
findings.change: Debounce-with-deadline. New volatile fields frontierBaseRebuildPending / frontierBaseRebuildPendingSinceNanos are set the first time runScheduledFrontierRebuild finds a base rebuild required (service.rebuildRequired(), the dimension flag, or a BASE_REBUILD_REQUIRED delta result) and cleared by clearFrontierBaseRebuildPending() after a successful base publish or an equivalent-generation abort. The pure FrontierRebuildSchedulePolicy.shouldStartBaseRebuild(now, lastRequest, pending, pendingSince, quietNanos, maxDeferralNanos) starts the rebuild when the 1 s quiet period has elapsed OR the pending rebuild has waited FRONTIER_REBUILD_MAX_DEFERRAL_NANOS = 5 s; differences of nanoTime are used so wrap-around is safe. The storeTxnStarted guard is unchanged (design open question kept as-is). While a base rebuild is pending, refreshFrontierStatisticsDelta still runs first every cycle so signed deltas keep publishing (RETRY/COMPLETE no longer short-circuit the rebuild branch). The debounce is preserved: a burst of five small commits followed by silence publishes 1..5 deltas and never a base rebuild (test). The secondary mapped/scalar flip (LmdbPackedCostModel.mappedStatisticsReady ignoring a complete in-memory tail) is deliberately deferred as the design recommends, since it needs tail-aware views; listed under followUps. One test expectation was corrected before the post-fix run: the burst test originally asserted exactly one delta, but deltas are not debounced by design (only base rebuilds are), so it now asserts 'no base rebuild, 1..5 deltas, no failure'. RESUMED SESSION 2026-09-28 (after the quota interruption; the tree now also carries the interrupted b3 edits: LmdbStatisticsService retirement GC, FrontierOmniIndex bridge orientation): all b2 production code was found complete and re-verified green; no production change was needed for this finding. Test-only change this session: steadySmallCommitsDoNotStarveARequiredBaseRebuild went red once in the class run (covered=0 after 12 s) while the machine ran at load 40 on 16 cores with the wt-wp8 and wt-wp6 core/sail/lmdb suites concurrently; the store shutdown then waited 36 s for the persist executor, i.e. the 20k-row base rebuild had started but was still running. Alone it passed in 11.95 s and the class rerun passed 6/6 under the same contention, so the 12 s coverage bound was measuring rebuild duration (load-dependent), not the scheduler. The assertion now bounds what the fix guarantees: the base rebuild must START within 8 s of the trickle beginning (5 s deferral deadline + 1 s scheduler tick + slack; detected by a base-builder build phase PASS_ONE/PASS_TWO/COMPACTING/PUBLISHING, an advanced baseEpoch or coverage), and coverage must arrive while commits continue at 4/s, with a 60 s outer bound; a per-poll status timeline is appended to the failure message. Under the old code neither assertion can pass (the rebuild never starts). This is a stronger statement of the starvation property, not a weakening.
